conviction_note: The reported quarter (calendar Q2 2026) is the one quarter in which both of this company's actual earnings drivers -- physical bar-and-coin volume and retail premium spread -- collapsed at once, which argues the single $0.96 estimate is too high; but I size it small because the only uncontaminated earnings reaction this registrant has ever produced was +0.95% on a 4.5x EPS beat, because the release is a full-year print that will read as a record by a factor of four, and because gold's July-August rally means management reports a stale bad quarter into a live good one.

findings.finding: Global bar-and-coin gold demand fell 36% sequentially to 307.1t in calendar Q2 2026 from 476.8t in Q1 -- and those are precisely the two quarters that map to Gold.com's fiscal Q4 (the quarter being reported, one estimate at $0.96) and fiscal Q3 (which printed $2.09), while retail premium spreads simultaneously troughed at multi-year lows and US Mint Silver Eagle bullion orders from Authorized Purchasers, of which A-Mark is one, hit exactly zero in May 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: This company's operating leverage is extreme and unmodelled by a one-estimate consensus: fiscal Q2 FY26 gross profit of $93.4m produced EPS of $0.46 while fiscal Q3's $176.6m produced $2.09, so an $83m gross-profit swing moved EPS by $1.63. Reverting Q4 gross profit toward the Q2 level on 36% lower volumes and compressed spreads puts EPS near $0.45-0.65, not $0.96. If the market had focused on this, the 20-day run-up would not be +2.3% -- the stock rose with gold through July and August while the volume and premium regime that actually sets its margin went the other way, which is the signature of a shareholder base pricing metal beta rather than dealer spread. There is also no sell-side preview to have carried it: coverage is effectively a single estimate, and the CEO's own Q2 FY26 language about 'tight' premium spreads in a quarter with better volumes than this one has never been connected to the Q4 setup in any published note.
findings.independence: Two further sources point the same way from different data: US Mint Authorized Purchaser orders for 1oz Silver Eagle bullion were zero for the whole of May 2026, the first full-month zero since the 1986 launch, with only ~260,000 in June (https://findbullionprices.com/blog/silver-eagle-sales-hit-zero-in-may-2026-the-retail-buyer-has-left/, corroborated independently at https://atlantagoldandcoin.com/us-mint-zero-silver-eagle-sales-may-2026/ -- both return 403 to automated fetch, so snippet-only); and Silver Eagle premium history shows the low print of 6.69% on 2026-05-25 against a ~19.2% peak earlier in 2026 (https://findbullionprices.com/premium-history/silver-coins/American-Silver-Eagle-Monster-Box-Random-Year/, snippet-only). A-Mark's Authorized Purchaser status is confirmed at https://www.usmint.gov/coins-precious-metal-coins/bullion-authorized-purchasers/. These are volume measures and a price measure respectively, so they are not restatements of the World Gold Council tonnage.

findings.finding: The baseline's two-print reaction history is half contaminated: the +9.87% move attributed to the 2026-02-05 amc earnings release was in fact the same-evening 4:10pm ET announcement of a $150m Tether PIPE at $44.50 with a board seat, alongside EPS of only $0.46 -- leaving 2026-05-06 (+0.95% on a sequential EPS jump from $0.46 to $2.09) as the only clean earnings reaction this registrant has produced.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a magnitude constraint, not a direction. The chain's 8.87% event-implied move and the baseline's 5.41% median absolute reaction both rest on treating February as an earnings reaction. Strip it and the demonstrated EPS-print sensitivity of this name is about one percent: the market was handed a 4.5x sequential EPS beat in May and moved the stock less than a point, because it correctly read the windfall as non-recurring. If the option market had made this adjustment, the ATM straddle would not be quoted with a bid-ask 62% of mid on 8,448 total open interest -- that width is what an uninterrogated volatility mark looks like. The market prices this stock off deals and narrative, which is exactly why the contamination happened in the first place.
findings.independence: The two-print history and the +0.95% May figure come from the sealed baseline, so the only genuinely independent leg is the release timestamp itself. The Q2 FY26 EPS of $0.46 that the +9.87% was mistakenly attributed to is at https://ir.gold.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/215/gold-com-reports-fiscal-second-quarter-2026-results (2026-02-05). Note this finding and finding 3 both lean on the 'market ignores this company's EPS line' reading of the same May 6 reaction -- treat them as one source cluster on that point.

findings.finding: Gold closed fiscal Q4 at $4,007.69 on 30 June 2026 and then rallied above $4,700 by 24 August -- its first move above $4,600 since 15 May -- before giving back 5.62% in the final week of August, and Silver Eagle premiums recovered from the 6.69% May trough to an 8.57% July average; so management reports a dead quarter into a rising, volatile one that resembles the regime that generated fiscal Q3's $2.09.
findings.why_not_priced: Gold's own level is obviously priced -- it is the most public number in the world, and GOLD's -6.8% five-day fade is simply beta to last week's 5.6% metal drop. What is not priced is the release's framing: this is a fiscal Q4 *and full-year* print in which the full year goes from $0.71 to roughly $3.20 in EPS and gross profit from $210.9m to roughly $450m, so the headline reads as a record by a factor of four while the soft quarter only appears in a sequential comparison that a one-analyst tape will be slow to compute. Had the market focused on the quarter rather than the year, the mildly positive 25-delta skew of +0.59 vol points would be materially wider on the put side than a flat market's half-point.
findings.independence: Independent corroboration of the July-August gold recovery and the late-August reversal at https://www.forbes.com/advisor/investing/gold-price/ (2026-08-31). The FY25 comparison base of $0.71 EPS and $210.9m gross profit is at https://ir.gold.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/206/a-mark-precious-metals-reports-fiscal-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results (2025-09-09). Shares the May 6 reaction reading with finding 2 -- see the note there.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR shows no 8-K, no executive-change filing and no pre-announcement between 2026-05-07 and 2026-09-02 on CIK 0001591588 -- a fully quiet 16 weeks into a full-year print, so no guidance revision or deal to trade
Layoffs, hiring-page deletions or team changes at Gold.com, JM Bullion, Monex, Goldline or Sunshine Minting -- nothing found in any channel
Reddit, Trustpilot and forum complaints about JM Bullion buyback payment delays, shipping backlogs or order problems -- nothing datable to the April-June 2026 quarter

Sunshine Minting step-acquisition accounting: the remaining 55.1% cost only ~$22.0m cash, implying ~$40m for the whole business, so any ASC 805 remeasurement gain on the previously held 44.9% is too small to move EPS against a $0.96 estimate

Secured lending loan book stress (337 loans, $126.0m receivable at 2026-03-31) -- no evidence of impairment or margin calls; gold at $4,000-4,300 is still far above any plausible origination collateral level
Tether PIPE dilution as a hidden EPS drag -- only ~1.3m incremental weighted shares versus Q3's 28,404,400 (~5%), partly offset by the enlarged 2026-04-08 buyback, and straightforward to model
The 2026-08-14 Schedule 13G (American Century, 1,644,385 shares / 5.7% as of 2026-06-30) -- routine passive accumulation, no signal

CEO Form 4 activity: Gregory Roberts sold 60,000 shares in May 2026 at ~$41.58-43.50 after option exercises at $1.63; he is a chronic exercise-and-sell filer, there is no cluster and the July 2026 Form 4 adds nothing directional
gold.com versus amark.com web traffic and customer-acquisition-cost evidence for the rebrand bet -- no usable public data

Whether May's zero Silver Eagle print was a Mint supply suspension rather than a demand collapse -- resolved against supply, because premiums were at multi-year lows and dealers were sitting on buyback inventory, but I could not fetch the primary usmint.gov bullion sales page (403)

A findbullionprices/Barchart piece headlined 'record-breaking demand meets lowest dealer premiums in years' looked like a perfect corroboration until the page itself dated it 2025-08-25 -- dropped, not used
baseline_tension: Finding 1 leans the same way as the mildly positive skew and the -6.8% five-day fade so it is partly in the price already, but finding 2 cuts hard against the 8.87% event-implied move by showing half the reaction history is not an earnings reaction at all, and the +2.3% twenty-day run-up through gold's July-August rally shows a market marking this name to metal beta rather than to the premium-and-volume regime that actually sets its gross margin.
